duomo: Cathedral, Baptistery and Piazza del Duomo

The cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, with Brunelleschi's great red dome, Giotto's bell tower and the Baptistery with its bronze doors. Entry to the cathedral is free: the interior is plain, with the Last Judgement frescoes inside the dome.
cupola: Dome, Bell Tower and Baptistery (Brunelleschi Pass)

The climb inside Brunelleschi's dome to the top, with the frescoes up close and the view over Florence's rooftops, then Giotto's bell tower, the Baptistery with its mosaics, the Opera del Duomo Museum and the crypt of Santa Reparata under the cathedral.
signoria: Piazza della Signoria and Palazzo Vecchio

Florence's civic square, with Palazzo Vecchio and its battlemented tower, the Loggia dei Lanzi with its statues (Cellini's Perseus), the Fountain of Neptune and the copy of David: the original is in the Accademia.
uffizi: Florence's largest art museum, in the Medici palace: Botticelli's Birth of Venus and Primavera, Leonardo's Annunciation, Michelangelo's Doni Tondo, plus Raphael, Caravaggio and Giotto. Two hours are enough for the masterpieces.
accademia: Michelangelo's David, over five metres tall, at the end of a gallery with the same artist's unfinished "Prisoners". It's a small museum: you see it all in an hour.
pontevecchio: The medieval bridge over the Arno with goldsmiths' shops hanging over the river. For the best photo, go to the nearby Ponte Santa Trinita and look at it from a distance, especially at sunset.
santacroce: The great Franciscan church with the tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli, Dante's cenotaph and Giotto's fresco cycles. Outside is one of the city's liveliest squares.
smn: The Dominican basilica opposite the station, with its white and green façade: inside are Masaccio's Trinity and Giotto's Crucifix, then the cloister with its frescoes.
piazzale: Piazzale Michelangelo and San Miniato al Monte

The viewpoint on the hill south of the Arno, overlooking all of Florence, the Cathedral and Palazzo Vecchio. A few minutes higher, at the top of the steps, is the Romanesque church of San Miniato al Monte with its white and green marble façade.
pitti: The Medici palace on the south bank of the Arno, with the Boboli Gardens behind it: avenues, fountains, statues and a great amphitheatre climbing the hill up to Forte Belvedere.
sanlorenzo: San Lorenzo, Mercato Centrale and the Medici Chapels

The market quarter: leather and souvenir stalls along the streets, the covered Mercato Centrale with its food counters, Brunelleschi's church of San Lorenzo and, at the back, the Medici Chapels with the Medici tombs and Michelangelo's sculptures.
santospirito: The artisans' quarter across the Arno: restoration workshops, frame-makers and marbled paper, Piazza Santo Spirito with Brunelleschi's church and the Florentines' own bars.
